candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly documents bilateral port-wine stains along V1/V2 distributions and brain MRI evaluation, which are hallmark features of Sturge-Weber syndrome. Ocular melanocytosis is a distinct entity (unilateral episcleral/uveal melanocytic proliferation) that does not encompass the cutaneous vascular birthmark or the syndromic diagnosis. While some ocular findings overlap, the candidate asserts a different diagnostic entity with an incompatible scope and etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ocular melanocytosis with glaucoma captures the ocular findings (iris hyperpigmentation, choroidal thickening, elevated IOP) but omits the defining systemic/cutaneous component (bilateral naevus flammeus along trigeminal divisions) and the neurological evaluation that together constitute Sturge-Weber syndrome

case_quality_flags: MRI negative for leptomeningeal involvement does not exclude Sturge-Weber syndrome; diagnosis rests on clinical criteria including port-wine stain distribution
Iris micronodular elevations and diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation are consistent with Sturge-Weber-associated ocular melanocytosis rather than standalone ocular melanocytosis
